capabilities: Watch a folder and transcribe new audio files via a local Docker backend
Categorize voice memos by filename prefixes and importance ratings
Generate per-note and weekly/monthly/yearly summaries with a local LLM
Record audio in-app and place it in the processing queue
Move finished transcripts to an output directory with metadata and tags
extras: Full backend setup, configuration and troubleshooting are documented in a separate obsidian-vox-backend repository; transcription is currently English-focused.
motivation: The author found that voice memos cannot be indexed or searched, and that a growing directory of audio files is no way to organize notes.
problem: Voice memos are not plaintext, so they cannot be searched, indexed or categorized, and a large folder of audio files becomes unmanageable.

relations.evidence: Vox requires a local backend to perform transcription. Head to obsidian-vox-backend
built-in AI summarization powered by a local LLM (Ollama)
The backend starts on and downloads the Whisper model (~470 MB)
sent directly to your desktop's backend over the encrypted Tailscale tunnel
Sync audio files to your desktop vault's watch folder using Syncthing

summary: Transcribes voice notes via a local Whisper backend and files them as categorized notes with frontmatter, tags and LLM-generated summaries.
